conviction_note: Nothing found that the market cannot already see. The 2026 guide only needs H2 service revenue of about -2% to +1% and H2 EBITDA of about -2% to +2% year on year, so a reaffirmation is very likely. Pulling the other way: Q3 is the first full quarter of the CRTC fee ban, it laps the MLSE consolidation (headline service-revenue growth falls from +8% to low single digits), it faces a tough Q3'25 net-add comparison (62k postpaid), and the Blue Jays' elimination sets up a weak Q4 media comparison. The October price increases are the main offset, but they are public and the stock is already up about 12% off its 9 October low. The findings sum to -0.45 and the scaled number is -0.14 (p_up 48 x abs 3.5); both are effectively zero.
bar: Company guide for FY2026, reaffirmed 2026-07-22 (https://about.rogers.com/wp-content/uploads/RCI-Q2-2026.pdf, slide 12): total service revenue +3% to +5% on 2025's C$19,104m, adjusted EBITDA +1% to +3% on C$9,820m, capex C$2.5-2.7bn, FCF C$4.1-4.3bn. The Q3 EPS consensus is NOT sourced reliably. AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517895-what-you-need-to-know-about-rogers-communications-incs-q3-earnings, 2026-10-21) gives US$0.80 from 14 estimates with 3 cut in the last 30 days, and the same page has internally inconsistent data. Benzinga's RCI pages show $0.86 and $0.93 in different editions. Two agreeing sources do not exist, so the EPS bar is unsourced and every reported-quarter finding is capped small. Year-ago comparison: Q3'25 adjusted EPS C$1.37, 62k postpaid / 111k total phone net adds, media revenue C$753m (MLSE already consolidated).
positioning_check: US-listed short interest 14.19m shares, 3.70% of float, 9.9 days to cover, as of the 2026-09-30 record date, up 3.7% from 13.68m (MarketBeat/FINRA, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/RCI/short-interest, published 2026-10-09). Not crowded; days to cover is high only because most volume trades on the TSX. Skew is not available: the chain is unusable (ATM spread 127% of mid, total OI 469). Put/call OI of 3.08 on that thin chain means nothing. Run-up: +3.12% over 5 days and +2.06% over 20 days at the seal; AAII reports +3.87% intraday on 2026-10-22 and +7.08% month to date off an October low of $29.255 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/467910-why-rogers-communications-inc8217s-rci-stock-is-up-955, 2026-10-22). Still -19.6% from the 52-week high and -12.6% year to date. AAII also reports 3 analyst estimate cuts in the prior month and none raised.

findings.finding: A reaffirmation of the 2026 guide is close to arithmetically assured. H1 2026 service revenue was about C$9.95bn (Q1 ~C$4.9bn +10%, Q2 C$5,055m +8%) and adjusted EBITDA about C$4.84bn (Q1 ~C$2.4bn +5%, Q2 C$2,442m +3%). The FY guide (service revenue C$19.68-20.06bn, EBITDA C$9.92-10.11bn) therefore needs H2 service revenue of only about -2.4% to +1.4% and H2 EBITDA of about -2% to +2% versus H2 2025. On FCF, H1 was about C$1.8bn (Q2 C$982m) against a C$4.1-4.3bn guide, so H2 needs C$2.3-2.5bn. Management said capex runs at about C$550m a quarter in H2 (Q2: C$695m) and that FCF growth 'further accelerates in the second half'. The market's expectation is a reaffirmation. A narrowing to the upper half is possible on revenue and EBITDA; FCF is the line that could disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was reaffirmed on 2026-07-22 and the stock still fell: -3.1% pre-market (RTTNews) and -4.13% per the baseline. The FCF guide was raised and capex cut on 2026-04-22, and the baseline reads -0.35%, which is unverified. The Q4'25 print with its first 2026 guide (2026-01-29) rose about +5% intraday (itiger).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Anyone can do this arithmetic, and a stock pricing a guide cut would sit lower than 4x P/E with three estimate cuts already in. What is not priced is a narrowing to the top of the range, which would show as a gap up on the release. The last reaffirmation was sold, so the reaction is sized small.
findings.independence: Q1 figures are from a separate document: https://www.globenewswire.com/fr/news-release/2026/04/22/3278812/0/en/rogers-communications-reports-first-quarter-2026-results.html (Q1 service revenue +10%, EBITDA +5%, FCF guide raised to C$4.1-4.3bn). The H2 FCF and capex commentary comes from the Q2 call transcript, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1926961-20260723, which is the same event as the deck.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first quarter that laps the MLSE consolidation, which began July 2025: Q3'25 media revenue was already C$753m including MLSE. Headline consolidated service-revenue growth therefore drops from +8% in Q2'26 (media +53%, of which +13% organic) to roughly low single digits in Q3. The deceleration is mechanical and sits inside the guide, but the headline revenue-growth optics turn sharply worse.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quarter lapped an acquisition this size. Q2'26 headline +8% service revenue with flat wireless service revenue was sold -4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models carry the lap, so it is largely priced. What is unpriced is how headline-reading flow responds to a release whose service revenue grows about 1-2% after two quarters of 8-10%. If that were fully priced, there would be no consensus-revenue confusion across aggregators, and there is (Benzinga carries a stale US$3.84bn).
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 deck (https://about.rogers.com/wp-content/uploads/RCI-Q2-2026.pdf, slide 4: media +53%, organic +13% ex MLSE) is a different document pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter under the CRTC ban on activation, modification and cancellation fees (Telecom Regulatory Policy 2026-43, effective 2026-06-12). Q2 mobile ARPU was already down 2% (C$54.25 vs C$55.45), partly on lower activation fees in the last weeks of the quarter. The CFO said he does not 'anticipate a substantial change' in the ARPU trajectory. Rogers' replacement C$40 device set-up charge, shipping fee and SIM fee are under CRTC review (Notice 2026-155), with possible fines of up to C$10m per violation. On 2026-09-23 management said ARPU pressure would last 'a few more quarters', with stabilisation in 2027. Market expectation: ARPU about -2%. The risk is a print nearer -3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 ARPU -2% with flat wireless service revenue: stock -4.13%. Q3'24, on wireless service-revenue pressure: -3.6% (Benzinga, Oct 2024).
findings.why_not_priced: Management pre-warned on direction, so the sign is priced. What is not priced is the size of the first full-quarter hit and whether the set-up fees offset it, which no public series measures. If it were priced, estimates would have been cut further than the 3 cuts AAII reports.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1926961-20260723 (fee change late in the quarter; ARPU trajectory flat). TMT conference summary, https://quartr.com/events/rogers-communications-inc-rci-2026-tmt-conference_3sOfKYFr (2026-09-23: ARPU pressure for a few more quarters). CRTC review: https://www.iphoneincanada.ca/2026/08/16/crtc-rejects-bell-rogers-telus-attempt-to-stall-switching-fee-probe/

findings.finding: Pricing turned up across the industry after quarter end. Bell raised its BYOD plans C$5-10 (entry 60GB plan to C$70) in early October 2026. Rogers and Telus followed on about 2026-10-09 with +C$5 on three of four main plans (Rogers 5G+ Lite C$65->70, Essentials C$70->75, Popular C$85->90). Bell also added C$6/month on affected existing Mobility plans from October billing. At the 2026-09-23 TMT conference management called the market 'stabilized, less discounting'. This is the Q4/2027 ARPU lever the call will be asked about, against an expectation of ARPU pressure 'for a few more quarters'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior. The stock's October low ($29.255) was on or near 2026-10-09, the day of the Rogers/Telus increase, and it has risen about 12% since. That suggests part of this is already in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, through the month-to-date rally. The unpriced part is management quantifying the back-book and front-book uplift, or moving the ARPU-stabilisation timing forward from '2027'. If fully priced, the stock would have recovered toward its 50-day average (C$49.21 on the TSX at 29 Sep) rather than sitting about 19% below its 52-week high.
findings.independence: Bell's back-book increase is separately reported at https://immigrationnewscanada.ca/bell-canada-price-increase-october-2026/ (2026-09-10; single-source, unverified). The TMT summary is a third document.

findings.finding: Wireless volumes face a tough comparison. Q2'26 postpaid phone net adds were 22k vs 35k a year earlier (40k total vs 61k), which management put down to a flat-to-declining population and 'lower end' 2% industry volume growth. The Q3'25 comparison is 62k postpaid and 111k total. A Q3 postpaid number well below 62k is expected. Partial offset: StatCan's September 2026 revision raised Canada's population by about 300k, with +80k in Q2 2026, reversing the 'declining population' narrative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 net adds -34% y/y: stock -4.13% (shared with the ARPU print, not separable). Q3'25 net adds of 111k with churn at a two-year low: shares up about 3% early (Reuters via stockopedia; year inferred).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because management guided volume to the low end. The population revision is a macro proxy the company has not confirmed. If the market had priced a volume collapse, the 3 recent estimate cuts would have been larger and the TMT 'stabilized' comment would have been challenged.
findings.independence: Q3'25 comparison: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/35631482/rogers-communications-reports-third-quarter-2025-results. Population revision: https://dailyhive.com/calgary/canada-population-statistics-update-september-2026 (proxy, cuts the other way).

findings.finding: The Blue Jays were eliminated from 2026 playoff contention on 2026-09-23 (77-81). The 2025 run reached World Series Game 7, Rogers' most-watched broadcast ever at 10.9m viewers, and inflated Q4'25 media revenue. Q4 2026 media therefore faces a steep comparison, and the Q3 call will frame it. Q3 itself was supported by 3.33m home attendance (41,220 per game), the second-best average in franchise history. Media is small in EBITDA (Q2'26: C$69m of C$2,442m), so net of the rest of the company this is a small outlook drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25, with the postseason media boost: +5% intraday on 2026-01-29. Q3'25 on media and sports strength: up about 3% early.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a month, and the stock fell about 7.7% in the week to 29 Sep, the week of the elimination. Probably mostly priced; what is left is management quantifying the Q4 media decline.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 Rogers priced US$1.0bn of 2057 fixed-to-fixed subordinated notes (US$500m at 7.150%, US$500m at 7.400%) and C$600m at 6.000%, closing 2026-09-23. The proceeds go to redeem the 5.00% notes due 2081 and/or the 5.25% notes due 2082. What the money buys: a refinancing of hybrid capital ahead of its call dates, which keeps rating-agency equity credit. It is not distress and not new spending. The cost is roughly C$30-40m a year of extra interest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 6-K day (2026-09-10 bmo) moved -0.96% per the baseline, which is a non-earnings row.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced; it was a public 6-K. It is filed because the higher coupon trims adjusted EPS and the 2027 interest-expense outlook by a few cents, which a reader of the Q3 release might notice.

findings.finding: The C$4.35bn purchase of Kilmer's 25% MLSE stake closed 2026-10-01, after quarter end. It was bridged with bilateral bank facilities, so pro forma leverage rises from 3.8x at June 30. Minority-stake proceeds are targeted for H1 2027 (a private placement in early 2027). Q2 carried a C$726m net loss from a non-cash revaluation of the MLSE put liability, and Q3 may carry a final remeasurement before extinguishment. The call will give the pro forma leverage path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: headline net loss of C$726m (adjusted EPS C$1.15 vs C$1.14 a year earlier) with a reaffirmed guide; stock -4.13%. Headline loss optics may have contributed.
findings.why_not_priced: The close and the funding are public. A remeasurement is non-cash and below operating income, so it is sized as a fraction. The unpriced part is the pro forma leverage number, which has not been published.
findings.independence: Q2 transcript, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1926961-20260723 (bank bridge, H1 2027 stake sale, leverage 3.8x). TMT summary (private placement early 2027).

findings.finding: The bar has been lowered and sector sentiment improved into the print. AAII (2026-10-21/22) reports 3 analysts cut Q3 estimates in the prior month and none raised. AT&T's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-21) showed its strongest service-revenue growth in more than four years and a raised 2026 EPS outlook. RCI rose +3.87% on 2026-10-22 to $32.98, +7.08% month to date. The lowered bar helps a beat on EPS; the US read-across is a weak proxy for Canada.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-print rallies: none verified. The prior print came off a weaker tape and was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-print rally means some of this is already in the price. The estimate cuts lower the bar the release is compared against, which matters only for the EPS headline. AAII's data is a single aggregator with inconsistencies.
findings.independence: AT&T Q3 2026 8-K exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000732717/000073271726000370/t-3q2026exhibit991.htm (2026-10-21). This is a proxy only; Rogers has no US operations.

outside_window.finding: Sale of a non-voting minority stake in the consolidated Rogers Sports entity (valued by Rogers at C$25bn+), with the private placement targeted for early 2027 and proceeds going to debt. The announcement is dated after the window, though call commentary may move it.

CRTC decision under Notice 2026-155 on whether Rogers' C$40 device set-up, shipping and SIM fees breach the fee ban (fines up to C$10m per violation; Telus has appealed procedure to the Federal Court of Appeal). No decision date is set.

baseline_tension: No skew is available. The baseline's reaction history is unusable (6-K rows), and rebuilt from confirmed prints it reads about -3.6% (Q3'24), +3% (Q3'25, early trading), +5% (Q4'25) and -4% (Q2'26), so the typical move is about 3.5% with no consistent sign. What I found is balanced: a mechanical guide reaffirmation and the October price increases against a first full quarter of the fee ban, the MLSE lap and tough net-add and media comparisons. The +7% pre-print rally puts p_up slightly below 50, given the name sold its last reaffirmation.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the guide-reaffirmation finding went from +0.4 to +0.3, because the 2026-07-22 reaffirmation was sold about 4%.
Rule 2 (one-offs): the MLSE put-liability / leverage finding went from -0.2 to -0.1, since a non-cash remeasurement below operating income is sized as a fraction.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): I asked what the September hybrid notes buy. The answer is a refinancing of 2081/2082 hybrids, not distress, so the finding went from -0.1 to -0.05.

Rule 5 and 6 (proxy, bar unsourced): the AT&T read-across and estimate-cut finding went from +0.3 to +0.2. The EPS bar has no two agreeing sources, so every reported-quarter finding stays capped small, and they already were.

Unreliable reaction history rule: I rebuilt the base rate from confirmed prints (Q3'24 -3.6%, Q3'25 about +3% early, Q4'25 +5%, Q2'26 -4.1%) and did not use the baseline's 0.75% median, so abs_move_pct stays at 3.5.
Unchanged: the ARPU/fee-ban, pricing, net-adds, MLSE-lap and Blue Jays findings.
